translation_en: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Yazid ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Every treacherous person will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection by which he will be recognized, and it will be said: This is the betrayal of so-and-so.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Every treacherous person will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection by which he will be recognized.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and 'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khulayd, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet, who said: Every treacherous person will have a banner at his backside on the Day of Resurrection.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us: al-Mustamir ibn al-Riyyan narrated to us: Abu Nadrah narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Every treacherous person will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection, raised in proportion to his treachery. Indeed, no treachery is greater than that of a ruler over the people.

'Ali ibn Hujr al-Sa'di, 'Amr al-Naqid, and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us. The wording is 'Ali's and Zuhayr's. 'Ali said: Sufyan informed us; the other two said: Sufyan narrated to us. He said: 'Amr heard Jabir say that the Messenger of Allah said: War is deception.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahm informed us: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: War is deception.

Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Hulwani and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hizami, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet said: Do not wish to meet the enemy. When you meet them, be steadfast.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Musa ibn 'Uqbah informed me, from Abu al-Nadr, from a letter written by a man from Aslam among the Prophet's Companions, called 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa. He wrote to 'Umar ibn 'Ubaydullah when he set out against the Haruriyyah, telling him that on one of the days when the Messenger of Allah met the enemy, he waited until the sun began to decline, then stood among the people and said: O people, do not wish to meet the enemy. Ask Allah for well-being. When you meet them, be steadfast and know that Paradise lies beneath the shade of swords. Then the Prophet stood and said: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Mover of the clouds, and Defeater of the confederates, defeat them and grant us victory over them.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: Khalid ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: The Messenger of Allah supplicated against the confederates, saying: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, swift in reckoning, defeat the confederates. O Allah, defeat them and shake them.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, who said: I heard Ibn Abi Awfa say that the Messenger of Allah supplicated against them with a prayer like Khalid's hadith, except he said: Defeater of the confederates. He did not mention the word O Allah at that point.
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Abi 'Umar both narrated this to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Isma'il, with this chain. Ibn Abi 'Umar added in his report: Mover of the clouds.

Hajjaj ibn al-Sha'ir narrated to me: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that on the day of Uhud the Messenger of Allah used to say: O Allah, if You will, You will not be worshipped on earth.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us. Another chain: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah: During one of the Messenger of Allah's campaigns, a woman was found killed. The Messenger of Allah condemned the killing of women and children.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Bishr and Abu Usamah narrated to us; they said: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: A woman was found killed during one of those campaigns, and the Messenger of Allah forbade killing women and children.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Sa'id ibn Mansur, and 'Amr al-Naqid all reported from Ibn 'Uyaynah. Yahya said: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubaydullah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah, who said: The Prophet was asked about the children of polytheists who are attacked at night and women and children are struck along with them. He said: They are of them.

'Abd ibn Humayd informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah, who said: I asked, Messenger of Allah, at night we may strike the children of polytheists. He said: They are of them.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: 'Amr ibn Dinar informed me that Ibn Shihab told him, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from al-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah, that the Prophet was asked: If cavalry attacked at night and struck the sons of the polytheists, what then? He said: They are of their fathers.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us. Another chain: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah: The Messenger of Allah burned the date palms of Banu al-Nadir and cut them down at al-Buwayrah. Qutaybah and Ibn Rumh add that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, revealed: Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah's permission, so that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient. The cited verse is 59:5.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah cut down and burned the date palms of Banu al-Nadir. Hassan said: A fire spread at al-Buwayrah, to the shame of the nobles of Banu Lu'ayy. Concerning this, the verse was revealed: Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, and the rest of the verse. The cited verse is 59:5.
Sahl ibn 'Uthman informed us: 'Uqbah ibn Khalid al-Sakuni informed me, from 'Ubaydullah, from Nafi', from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah burned the date palms of Banu al-Nadir.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ma'mar. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rafi'—the wording is his—narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah. Among those reports he said: A prophet among the prophets went on a campaign and told his people: No man who has married a woman and has not yet consummated the marriage should follow me; nor a man who has built a house but not yet raised its roof; nor a man who has bought sheep or pregnant camels and is waiting for their offspring. He went on campaign and approached a town around the time of the afternoon prayer. He said to the sun: You are commanded and I am commanded. O Allah, hold it back for me for a while. It was held back until Allah granted him victory. They gathered the spoils, but a fire came to consume them and refused to touch them. He said: There is embezzlement among you. Let one man from each tribe pledge allegiance to me. They did so, and one man's hand stuck to his. He said: There is embezzlement among you; let your tribe pledge allegiance to me. They did, and the hands of two or three men stuck to his. He said: You have embezzled; there is embezzlement among you. They brought him gold about the size of a cow's head and placed it with the goods on the ground. The fire came and consumed them. Spoils had not been lawful for anyone before us. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, saw our weakness and inability, so He made them lawful for us.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Simak, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from his father, who said: My father took a sword from the fifth of the spoils and brought it to the Prophet, saying: Give this to me. He refused, and Allah, Mighty and Exalted, revealed: They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger. The cited verse is 8:1.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. They said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from his father, who said: Four verses were revealed concerning me. I got hold of a sword and brought it to the Prophet, saying: Messenger of Allah, award it to me. He said: Put it down. He stood, and the Prophet told him: Put it back where you took it. He got up again and asked for it. The Prophet said: Put it down. He got up and said: Messenger of Allah, award it to me. Am I to be treated like someone with no merit? The Prophet said: Put it back where you took it. Then this verse was revealed: They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger. The cited verse is 8:1.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: al-Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Simak ibn Harb narrated to us: Mus'ab ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from his father, that verses of the Quran were revealed concerning him. He said: Sa'd's mother swore she would never speak to him until he disbelieved in his religion, and she would neither eat nor drink. She said: You claim Allah instructed you to treat your parents well, and I am your mother, commanding you to do this. She remained like that for three days until she fainted from exhaustion. Her son 'Umarah got up and gave her drink, and she began praying against Sa'd. Then Allah revealed the verse: We have instructed the human being to treat his parents well, and: If they strive to make you associate with Me, and: Keep their company in this world with kindness. Sa'd said: The Messenger of Allah gained a great amount of spoils, including a sword. I took it and brought it to the Messenger, saying: Award me this sword; you know my situation. He said: Return it to where you took it. I left, but when I was about to put it among the collected goods, I blamed myself and returned, asking him to give it to me. He raised his voice and said: Return it to where you took it. Then Allah revealed: They ask you about the spoils. Sa'd said: I became ill and sent for the Prophet. He came, and I asked him to let me distribute my property however I wished. He refused. I asked for half; he refused. I asked for one third; he remained silent, and afterward one third was permitted. Sa'd said: I went to a group of the Ansar and Emigrants, who said: Come, we will feed you and give you wine. This was before wine was forbidden. I went to a garden, where they had a roasted camel's head and a skin of wine. I ate and drank with them. They mentioned the Ansar and Emigrants, and I said the Emigrants were better than the Ansar. A man took a jawbone and struck me with it, splitting my nose. I went to the Messenger of Allah and told him. Then Allah revealed concerning me the ruling on wine: Wine, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are filth from Satan's work. The cited references are 29:8, 31:15, 8:1, and 5:90.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from his father, who said: Four verses were revealed concerning me. He related the hadith with the meaning of Zuhayr's report from Simak. Shu'bah's report adds that when they wanted to give Sa'd's mother something to drink, they forced her mouth open with a stick and poured it down her throat. It also says the blow split Sa'd's nose, which remained split.

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Prophet sent out a detachment, and I was among them, toward Najd. They gained many camels. Each man's share was twelve or eleven camels, and they were additionally given one camel each.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us. Another chain: Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah sent a detachment toward Najd, including Ibn 'Umar. Their shares reached twelve camels, and they were additionally given one camel. The Messenger of Allah did not change this.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir and 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah sent a detachment to Najd, and I went with it. We captured camels and sheep. Our shares amounted to twelve camels, and the Messenger of Allah gave us one camel each as an additional award.
Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya, al-Qattan, narrated to us, from 'Ubaydullah, with this chain.

Abu al-Rabi' and Abu Kamil narrated this to us: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub. Another chain: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, who said: I wrote to Nafi' asking him about the additional award from spoils. He wrote back that ... Another chain: Ibn Rafi' narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Musa informed me. Another chain: Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah ibn Zayd informed me. All reported from Nafi' with this chain, with a report like theirs. The source includes the number 4661.
